disclaimer: This report lists observations and unconfirmed hypotheses derived from captured evidence. WHD does not assert a root cause. Hypotheses are starting points for the listed follow-up tests.

observations.text: 2089 events analyzed, 33 significant (severity ≥ warning or state-changing kinds), 10 at warning or above; 1 incident(s) (events within 8s of each other).
8 event(s) carry no device attribution (e.g. kernel printk lines without a device prefix); they are included in time-based incident clustering but not assigned to a device.
pci:0000:07:00.0:14c3:7927: PCIe link 8.0 GT/s PCIe x1 (maximum 8.0 GT/s PCIe x1); at maximum.
pci:0000:07:00.0:14c3:7927: ASPM L0s off, L1 off (decoded from Link Control).
pci:0000:07:00.0:14c3:7927: driver mt7925e_git (module mt7925e_git), firmware ____000000-20260414134255, out-of-tree module (taint O).
Incident I1 (error, 11.7s, 33 events): first significant event per layer in observed order: bus@+0s → firmware@+7.833s → mac80211@+8.967s → netdev@+9s.
MCU timeout ('firmware.mcu_timeout') at +24.0s followed by 'reset.chip_reset' 0.03s later after 1 retry message(s).
Bus-level event(s) preceded the MCU timeout in the same incident: pci.aer.received — the bus may be the initiator rather than the firmware.

sequence.summary: AER correctable counters increased: BadTLP+2, TOTAL_ERR_COR+2

hypotheses.title: MCU/firmware stopped answering host commands
hypotheses.statement: In 1 incident(s) an MCU command timed out and the driver then reset the chip. This is consistent with the firmware (or the host↔firmware command path) becoming unresponsive. The evidence places the boundary at the host driver ↔ MCU command channel, not at the radio or the network.
unknowns: Whether the firmware crashed, hung on one command, or the DMA/interrupt path stalled: all produce the same log lines.
Why the command was sent at that moment (what triggered it).
Whether a bus fault happened without being logged (corrected AER is rate-limited/not logged).

missing_instrumentation.why_it_matters: Recovery duration and the stage that failed are only inferable from log text.
missing_instrumentation.proposal: Proposal only (no diff): mt792x:reset_stage tracepoints around the recovery sequence.

missing_instrumentation.what: Device attribution for custom driver printk lines
missing_instrumentation.why_it_matters: 8 event(s) cannot be tied to a specific adapter; with several adapters, per-device analysis misses them.
missing_instrumentation.proposal: Use dev_info()/dev_dbg() (device-prefixed) for driver debug lines; WHD attributes by prefix.

follow_ups.title: Capture MCU command lifecycle around the failure
follow_ups.how: Apply the optional mt76 tracepoint patch (docs/patches/0001) to a build you control, then run a WHD capture with trace events mt76/mcu_send,mcu_resp. Shows which command stalled and prior latencies.
follow_ups.whd_feature: mt76 tab → Instrumentation coverage → patch proposals

follow_ups.title: Compare PCIe AER counters and status before/after an incident
follow_ups.how: Device → Bus tab shows AER counters (sysfs) and, with the helper, decoded AER registers. Note whether uncorrectable status bits or fatal counters change at the failure instant.

follow_ups.title: Repeat the capture under the same workload
follow_ups.how: Run another capture of equal length with the same traffic. Compare incident count and interval (Diagnostics → patterns). Repeatability separates a systematic fault from a one-off.

limits: Timestamps come from different clocks: kernel printk (µs, converted with the current CLOCK_BOOTTIME offset; off by any suspend time), tracefs boot clock (ns), and WHD receive time for netlink/uevent events. Events from sysfs polling are accurate only to the polling interval (2 s).
Only events WHD received are analyzed; WHD has no kernel history from before it started except the journal backfill, and journald/ratelimit can drop messages.
Hypotheses use fixed, documented rules; absence of a hypothesis does not mean absence of a problem.
